Come as a guest, leave as a friend.

neighborhood_overview: Officially the smallest neighborhood in the City of Boston, Bay Village more than makes up for its lack of size with its inviting and friendly atmosphere. (The locals chat and wave to each other.) Created by a landfill in the 1820's by developer Ephraim Marsh, many of the homes look like smaller versions of Beacon Hill townhouses because the craftspeople who built the Beacon Hill residences settled in this area and built residences for their own use. The neighborhood is little known, but very centrally located nestled between the Back Bay, South End, and Theater District.

neighborhood_overview:
Jamaica Plain is one of the most fun and funky residential neighborhoods of Boston. It was one of the "streetcar suburbs" which were settled when the streetcars extended out from Boston in the mid-1800s, and most of the housing is Victorian, dating from about 1860 on. Let me know what brings you to Boston and what your interests are and I will do my very best to enhance your experience and make your stay in one of America’s most distinctive, charming, and authentic  urban neighborhoods unforgettable. We're close to the airport, which is super convenient. You can sometimes hear the planes but it's not a nuisance (we've lived here for 10 years and love it).

East Boston is a place that immigrants from all over the world (most commonly Central American and North African), young urban professionals, and old-school Italian-American families call home.

We moved here 10 years ago, never expecting to stay, but we fell in love with the neighborhood. It's not glitzy or glamorous, but you will find delicious restaurants, good people, and a charming, relaxed city neighborhood. The food/restaurant scene ranges from Italian to Central American and Mexican, from North African to Australian meat pies—all within walking distance.

neighborhood_overview:
The South End neighborhood of Boston is recognized by the National Register of Historic Places as the oldest and largest Victorian neighborhood in the country. The neighborhood is home to many fine restaurants, cafes, galleries, shops, and bars. It is very walkable and ideal for sightseeing at many attractions. There are eleven parks nearby, perfect for a relaxing after dinner stroll.
Despite becoming very gentrified in the past 30 years, the location has a rich history of attracting diverse groups of people. The neighborhood was originally built in 1849 on tidal marshes to divert the city’s population from the crowded downtown and Beacon Hill neighborhoods. The first waves of residents included new immigrants residing in rooming houses (more likely than not, our house was one!), followed by a burgeoning middle class that included business owners and bankers. In the 1920s, settlement houses were being built as a way for the city to bring people of different socio-economic classes

description: Large bedroom in a classic Boston brownstone in a historic district. Walk everywhere and just 3 minutes by foot to the subway! neighborhood_overview:
The South End neighborhood of Boston is recognized by the National Register of Historic Places as the oldest and largest Victorian neighborhood in the country. The neighborhood is home to many fine restaurants, cafes, galleries, shops, and bars. It is very walkable and ideal for sightseeing at many attractions. There are eleven parks nearby, perfect for a relaxing after dinner stroll.
Despite becoming very gentrified in the past 30 years, the location has a rich history of attracting diverse groups of people. The neighborhood was originally built in 1849 on tidal marshes to divert the city’s population from the crowded downtown and Beacon Hill neighborhoods. The first waves of residents included new immigrants residing in rooming houses (more likely than not, our house was one!), followed by a burgeoning middle class that included business owners and bankers. In the 1920s, settlement houses were being built as a way for the city to bring people of different socio-economic classes

name: Cozy Back Bay Boston Retreat!
description: There is not a better location in the city with quick and easy access to everything Boston has to offer, as well as the neighboring communities. You will find the space to be a little sanctuary away from the hustle and bustle of city life whether you are in Boston for work or leisure. Much like rest of Back Bay, the space and finishes have a Victorian era feel with some updates made throughout the decades. I hope you can relax and feel at home!
neighborhood_overview:
Back Bay is an affluent shopping and dining destination that abuts some of the greatest neighborhoods and areas in the city. Home to Newbury Street - where locals and tourists frequent designer boutiques, fashion chains, art galleries and patio cafes set in elegant brick townhouses. A quick and easy walk to the Kenmore/Fenway area via Beacon Street, as well as a short stroll down the Comm Ave. Mall (long strip of grass) to the Boston Common.

You have quick an easy access to major highways (I-90 and I-93) and local thorough-fares (Storrow Drive and Memorial Drive). With a quick 15-minute ride from Logan International Airport, as well as North and South Station within 10-minutes away, access to the city couldn't be easier. Further, Boston was made for walking, so take advantage if you are able!
host_about: I am a big traveler and love to discover the local flavor of any place I visit. Born and raised north of Boston, but lived most my adult life in the DC area. Moved back to Boston a couple years ago and have loved the continued transformation of such a historically rich city. So much has changed from my grandparents Boston to what you’ll experience today and it is all so exciting. The food, entertainment, arts, sports, shopping, outdoors, indoors...there is an energy in the city that is hard to miss. I hope you enjoy the city and everything it has to offer. I typically experience new places by hitting the street via walking or running and Boston couldn’t be a better city for just that. Enjoy and have fun!!

host_about:
Welcome!

I moved to Boston nine years ago after having lived for more than 30 years in three different countries on as many continents.  I have a passion for travelling  and, since my migration to Boston, have so enjoyed the experience of hosting other travelers through Airbnb (in addition to a non-paying website.)  I love that people from vastly different corners of the world and its multiple paths  arrive on my doorstep; I also love being of service, and sharing my resources (including my cats. :-)

I'm an educator, artist, (vegetarian) cook, polyglot, nature-lover, film aficionado, social-justice activist, and mother to three enchanting fur-people.  I try my modest best to live with care, consciousness and compassion.  My nest is my castle and, whether you're here on holiday, or for a work gig,  I would hope that it's a kind of "home away from home" for you.

neighborhood_overview:
The South End neighborhood of Boston is recognized by the National Register of Historic Places as the oldest and largest Victorian neighborhood in the country. The neighborhood is home to many fine restaurants, cafes, galleries, shops, and bars. It is very walkable and ideal for sightseeing at many attractions. There are eleven parks nearby, perfect for a relaxing after dinner stroll.
Despite becoming very gentrified in the past 30 years, the location has a rich history of attracting diverse groups of people. The neighborhood was originally built in 1849 on tidal marshes to divert the city’s population from the crowded downtown and Beacon Hill neighborhoods. The first waves of residents included new immigrants residing in rooming houses (more likely than not, our house was one!), followed by a burgeoning middle class that included business owners and bankers. In the 1920s, settlement houses were being built as a way for the city to bring people of different socio-economic classes

Warmest regards

Sue

name: Modern Smart 1Bdr Private Entry Historic South End
description:
Fully Automated Smart Home with Private Entry. Boston's best Location. Clean, recently renovated historic home, close to everything.

We have sought to equip a home to a high standard and to anticipate your needs for a luxurious stay beyond imagination. You talk and it listens. It's a very Special Suite that makes your home away from home! We have made an effort to make the Suite feel like a self-serving and comfort retreat. We hope you enjoy our piece of paradise. Sit back and relax
neighborhood_overview:
Enjoy this amazing in high demand historic neighborhood of Boston where you can eat and shop! Come home to sleep in our smart, voice command, ready to dazzle your one-bedroom suite! The South End of Boston has the most popular trendy cafes and restaurants. Also, it is close to everywhere. Walk to places, take an easy short ride, or use the T to get to places in a very short period of time.
Enjoy a private space to call home during your Boston stay! A luxurious smart apartment with full bath eating kitchen in an amazing location. You won't find any other place like this!
host_about:
I am an Artist who has lived in Boston all my life. I love living in the city, but also enjoy getting away for work or visiting my husband’s relatives in Greece.

I have been renting my apartments for decades, although furnished now, I know how important it is to make your stay easy and comfortable. Your accommodations are exactly as advertised. The amenities are as luxurious as our former wonderful guests specify. The apartment is short term rental specifically designed for your total comfort. As our guests mentioned "The pictures don’t do it any justice."

My husband Alex and I take the feedback we have gotten from our initial guests very seriously, and have implemented all suggestions to improve the apartment and the experience…. Even though all of our reviews are very positive, we strive to always improve ourselves and our apartments.

As a host, we will be as involved with your trip as much as you want. If you would like to get recommendations as to where to go, what to do, and places to eat we will most certainly help you with that, but if you rather be left alone, we will let you enjoy your privacy of your own apartment while visiting Boston.

Enjoy your visit to Boston and when you are finished with your day of tourism or work, you can return to your rental home. REST and RELAX in a clean and well-appointed apartment. The goal is that you have a worry free and comfortable stay. 

Welcome to Boston and its historic South End!

Sincerely,
Stephanie & Alex

Once its own city, Dorchester is now Boston’s largest and most diverse neighborhood, evident in the wide variety of global cuisines found on Dorchester Avenue. The district hosts UMass Boston and the John F. Kennedy Presidential Library, with artifacts from the president’s life and exhibits on the civil rights era. The Neponset River meanders past several parks, and nearby Franklin Park has woodland trails and a zoo.

Since the early 1900s, the area along Washington and Tremont Streets, roughly from School Street to Beach Street, has also been referred to as the Ladder District. Now it is most commonly named Downtown Crossing as most of the city's Subway's or (T-lines) intersect at Park Street station. The MBTA's Downtown Crossing subway station directly serves Downtown Crossing. The State Street and Park Street stations are within close walking distance. Silver Line service is also available. You can get literally anywhere in the city for a few dollars and a Tpass.

The apartment building is located on a dead end street which means it's super quiet for automobile traffic, but still has the lively city feel as foot traffic is sure to be noticeable any time of day, even in the winter. The Boston Common is only a few hundred feet from the entrance to the building.

Escape the hustle and bustle of the city and unwind aboard Carpe Diem II, a yacht with 2 comfy queen staterooms for up to 4 adults. Each stateroom has a private bathroom and shower.
Unwind on the aft deck with meals and cocktails as the boats sail by on the harbor, or warm up or cool off inside with central A/C and heat.
Located in Charlestown Navy Yard, steps to Freedom Trail, North End, and Downtown. Book now and enjoy the unique charm of living on the water in this historic neighborhood.
neighborhood_overview:
MV Carpe Diem II provides an expansive view of the Boston skyline and wonderful sea breezes. Located in Charlestown, the oldest neighborhood in the US, is full of history.

* 5 min walk to the USS Constitution
* 10 min walk to the Bunker Hill Monument
* 5 min walk to the Freedom Trail
* 15 min walk to the North End (Ferry service available as well!)
* 20 min walk Downtown and Faneuil Hall
* 10 min walk to the TD Garden
* 20 min Uber/Taxi to Fenway Park
* 15 min Water Taxi ride to Seaport

Logan Airport:
10-15 minute Uber/Lyft/Taxi Ride
20-30 minute Water Taxi Ride
host_about:
I'm a small business owner, born and raised in NH. 6 shops with 15 employees. Love to travel, scuba dive, boat and play hockey. I live on a houseboat full time and love it! 
I love sharing my love of the water and Boston with others. Staying on a boat is one of the coolest ways to see a city and one of the best nights sleep you’ll ever have. 
I’m here to help you make sure your stay in Boston is the best it can possibly be. I’m happy to make any and all suggestions to make sure you can experience “the town” like a local.

Jamaica Plain (known as JP by locals) is a family friendly town a hop and a skip away from Boston... In the immediate neighborhood (a 5-12 minute walk radius) there is a CVS , Chilacates (mexican takeout); a local corner market; a local no-contracts gym; Ula’s (coffeeshop); the Sam Adams brewery.

neighborhood_overview:
Dorchester, colloquially referred to as Dot, is the City of Boston's largest, most populous, and most diverse neighborhood where long-time residents mingle together with immigrants from Vietnam, Cape Verde, Ireland, and many other countries. The wonderful mix of residents from all cultures and backgrounds makes it an incredibly vibrant place to live, work, and spend time.

The house is located between the Savin Hill and Fields Corner sections of Dorchester (it is also of similar distances, about 10-15 minutes walking, to the Savin Hill and Fields Corner subway stations). Savin Hill, to the North, is home to Savin Hill beach and local favorite brunch sport McKenna’s Café. Fields Corner, to the South, is Dorchester's busiest commercial district where you can find restaurants serving cuisines from the Caribbean, Ireland, Latin America, and Vietnam.

The South Bay center, which is a 5-10 minute drive from the house, is a large mix-use area with more than 30 retailers

Allston can be reached via the “B” Branch of the MBTA Green Line.

host_about:
I graduated college in 2017 with a chemistry degree. During college, I picked up a part time job as a houseman in my school’s hotel, less so for the money. More so to look busy. It was initially meant to be a past time, but one particular night left a mark I never forgot.

The job required me to assist the housekeepers. I was the grease to a well-maintained machine. Take off the bed sheets, remove the used soaps and towels, and empty the trash. You do that to every room. Simple right?

It was the last night for an opposing school’s football team and my manager needed someone to clean up after them and then prepare the rooms for the next working day.

I showed up and cleared every room assigned to me. I thought nothing of it and went back to my dorm. The next day, I went back to work on my regular shift. 

To my surprise, everyone came up to me to thank me for making their day a hundred times easier. I was happy for a moment. But then I scratched my head thinking to myself, “you all know that I’m getting paid for this right?”

neighborhood_overview:
Beacon Hill is located in the center of Boston and teems with historic charm. The meticulously maintained rowhouses date back to the late 1700s, and the narrow gas-lit streets feature beautifully crafted doors, brick and cobblestone sidewalks, and flower boxes. The neighborhood is home to the Massachusetts State House and a passageway from the underground railway. While mostly residential, Beacon Hill also has a commercial area (Charles Street) which features great restaurants and boutique shopping.

Beacon Hill is a walker's paradise, neighboring Downtown, North End, Back Bay, and the Boston Common and Public Garden. If you'd like to explore more of greater Boston, you can access all four lines of the T (Boston's subway) within a 5-10 min walk.

My  house is 2 miles to Harvard School of Medicine, Longwood Medical area, Northeastern and a bit further but not far the medical campus of Boston University, 10 min T ride from Back Bay where you can find The Arquitectural School and MFA is 2.3 miles away.

host_about:
I live in Boston and like to do short trips to cities in many countries. I work as a consultant all over the world.
I believe that wasting time is a good thing, we are overscheduled, overinvolved, and overstretched. Traveling allows me to kick back and go to museum just because. Or sit in café, if I am too tired for a museum, or do both.
My favorite city is Barcelona, although Boston great, too, and so is Buxtehude, my home town in Germany. I believe you can find beautiful things in almost all cities, and in the end it is more about whom you travel with and whom you meet. 
My girlfriend and I just started hosting, but already had guests from many parts of the world.

Many wise people have said many wise things. There is a German saying "If you say A, you also have to say B", which is to say that you have to follow through if you have started something. Einstein responded to that: "If you say A, you don't need to say B, you can also see that A was wrong". How about that for humbleness of an atheist. Well, I wasn't there when he said it, but this is what lore has ..
Between my girlfriend and me, we can help you with German, English, French , Chinese, some Spanish and some Japanese. 
We explicitly welcome people from every corner of the world, and everyone who believes in respect and love for all others.

name: Charming and Historic Apartment
description:
Located in the heart of the historic Beacon Hill neighborhood, this cozy apartment is on the first two floors of a four-story brick townhouse. Tucked away on a European-style gated courtyard, the apartment is incredibly quiet and private, and only steps away from the shops, restaurants and public transportation of Charles Street and Cambridge Street.

The well equipped kitchen has been recently renovated with free in unit laundry, bar, adjacent patio. Also WFH station and gas fireplace.
neighborhood_overview:
Beacon Hill is an incredibly charming and fun neighborhood. The apartment is located within steps of the famous Cambridge and Charles streets, that are both full of shops, restaurants, coffee shops and more. A stroll down Charles Street ends in the beautiful Boston Common and Public Garden.

Back Bay, Downtown, historic sites, and the North End are all easily in walking distance. The Charles/MGH T station (red line) is one block from the apartment providing quick and easy access to Cambridge, Harvard, South Station and the Seaport.

MGH hospital / ER is just one block away. Whole Foods grocery store and CVS are an 8 minute walk; other local markets are a 5 minute walk. Plenty of local bars and cuisine to choose from for breakfast, lunch and dinner!
host_about:
Hello and welcome to my home! I’ve lived in Boston for over 20 years and have been on Beacon Hill for the last 5. I love the charm, beauty and history of the neighborhood and this city. There is no other place like it!

I am a competitive sailboat racer so I know Boston Harbor and Massachusetts Bay very well. I am a member of the Beacon Hill Civic Association and volunteer as a tour guide!  I’m happy to provide recommendations, so just ask!

Once its own city, Dorchester is now Boston’s largest and most diverse neighborhood, evident in the wide variety of global cuisines found on Dorchester Avenue. The district hosts UMass Boston and the John F. Kennedy Presidential Library, with artifacts from the president’s life and exhibits on the civil rights era. The Neponset River meanders past several parks, and nearby Franklin Park has woodland trails and a zoo.

Dorchester is also home to Franklin Park, the “crown jewel” of the Emerald Necklace Park System. The park has more 527 acres of green space, a zoo, and public golf course. Among the dozens of other parks in the neighborhood, recently renovated Pope John Paul II Park offers numerous walking and bike paths, athletic fields, and picnic areas with beautiful views of Boston Harbor and the Neponset River.

The North End is Boston's oldest residential neighborhood and could best be described as the "Little Italy" of Boston. The North End is one of the most visited neighborhoods in the City of Boston and is the hub of the Italian-American community. It’s character is woven through the neighborhoods narrow yet vibrant streets that boast some of the best restaurants and old world cafes the City has to offer. host_about:
I graduated college in 2017 with a chemistry degree. During college, I picked up a part time job as a houseman in my school’s hotel, less so for the money. More so to look busy. It was initially meant to be a past time, but one particular night left a mark I never forgot.

The job required me to assist the housekeepers. I was the grease to a well-maintained machine. Take off the bed sheets, remove the used soaps and towels, and empty the trash. You do that to every room. Simple right?

It was the last night for an opposing school’s football team and my manager needed someone to clean up after them and then prepare the rooms for the next working day.

I showed up and cleared every room assigned to me. I thought nothing of it and went back to my dorm. The next day, I went back to work on my regular shift. 

To my surprise, everyone came up to me to thank me for making their day a hundred times easier. I was happy for a moment. But then I scratched my head thinking to myself, “you all know that I’m getting paid for this right?”

But then it dawned on me. I was looking at this experience through broken glasses.

Hospitality is as much a human experience for the guests as it is for the people who make that experience worthwhile. 

That day has inspired to me to strive to make every experience worthwhile. My goal is to facilitate wonderful experiences for people around the world. Hopefully, hosting on Airbnb will be the catalyst for my guests to make fun, happy, and joyful memories.

Downtown Boston’s Faneuil Hall area is a vibrant blend of history and modern city life. As a key stop along the Freedom Trail, this neighborhood is rich in historical significance, featuring landmarks such as Quincy Market and the Old State House. Faneuil Hall, often called “the Cradle of Liberty,” offers lively street performers, outdoor markets, and a variety of dining options.

The area is bustling with shops, cafés, and restaurants serving everything from local seafood to global cuisine. Government Center, located just steps away, serves as a major civic hub and gateway to the area’s attractions. Visitors can easily explore nearby highlights like the New England Aquarium and the Rose Kennedy Greenway. This walkable and well-connected part of the city combines Boston’s rich history with its contemporary culture, delivering a dynamic urban experience.

host_about:
I graduated college in 2017 with a chemistry degree. During college, I picked up a part time job as a houseman in my school’s hotel, less so for the money. More so to look busy. It was initially meant to be a past time, but one particular night left a mark I never forgot.

The job required me to assist the housekeepers. I was the grease to a well-maintained machine. Take off the bed sheets, remove the used soaps and towels, and empty the trash. You do that to every room. Simple right?

It was the last night for an opposing school’s football team and my manager needed someone to clean up after them and then prepare the rooms for the next working day.

I showed up and cleared every room assigned to me. I thought nothing of it and went back to my dorm. The next day, I went back to work on my regular shift. 

To my surprise, everyone came up to me to thank me for making their day a hundred times easier. I was happy for a moment. But then I scratched my head thinking to myself, “you all know that I’m getting paid for this right?”

But then it dawned on me. I was looking at this experience through broken glasses.

Hospitality is as much a human experience for the guests as it is for the people who make that experience worthwhile. 

That day has inspired to me to strive to make every experience worthwhile. My goal is to facilitate wonderful experiences for people around the world. Hopefully, hosting on Airbnb will be the catalyst for my guests to make fun, happy, and joyful memories.

host_about:

We are partnered with a wonderful non-profit that specializes in providing  housing for families in need of a discounted or free place to stay for the duration of their hospital visits. We hope we get the chance to host you!

Harvard Square (8-minute drive):

Harvard Square isn’t just a place – it’s a storybook of American history and culture with pages that unfold at every corner. This area has been a meeting point for intellectuals, artists, and revolutionaries for centuries. It was the site of the first printing press in British North America in 1638, producing works like the “Bay Psalm Book”. During the abolitionist movement, the square was a hub for activism and later a focal point for anti-war protests in the 20th century.

Key attractions include the Harvard Art Museums, where you can view masterpieces by Vincent van Gogh (Self-Portrait Dedicated to Paul Gauguin), Claude Monet (La Japonaise), and Georgia O’Keeffe (Red Hills, Grey Sky). Nearby, the Harvard Museum of Natural History showcases the renowned Glass Flowers collection, intricately crafted models of over 4,000 plant species​

For bookworms, the Harvard Book Store is a literary paradise with shelves of rare find
